deep.reconstruction:
The page is a scratch sheet with three separate threads.

(1) TOP: spherical-triangle discriminant. Gauss expands (cos a - cos b cos c)^2 - sin^2 b sin^2 c.
- First expansion: cos^2 a - 2 cos a cos b cos c + cos^2 b cos^2 c - (1 - cos^2 b)(1 - cos^2 c).
- He jots the leftover pieces as the lines 'cos b^2', '-1', 'cos c^2'. The terms cos^2 b cos^2 c cancel.
- With alpha = cos a, beta = cos b, gamma = cos c the result is alpha^2 + beta^2 + gamma^2 - 2 alpha beta gamma - 1. He writes this as the pair of rows 'alpha alpha + beta beta + gamma gamma - 2 alpha beta gamma' and '+1 - alpha alpha - beta beta - gamma gamma'.
- So the bracket equals -(1 - alpha^2 - beta^2 - gamma^2 + 2 alpha beta gamma).
- [my gloss] By the cosine rule, cos a - cos b cos c = sin b sin c cos A. The quantity is therefore -sin^2 b sin^2 c sin^2 A, i.e. minus the Gram determinant of the three unit vectors of the triangle.
- The next two rows read '(1+) alpha^2 beta^2 + beta^2 gamma^2 + alpha^2 gamma^2 (+ alpha beta gamma) - 2 alpha beta gamma - alpha^2 beta^2 gamma^2'. The leading '1+' is struck. This matches (1-alpha^2)(1-beta^2)(1-gamma^2) - (1 - alpha^2 - beta^2 - gamma^2 + 2 alpha beta gamma) = alpha^2 beta^2 + beta^2 gamma^2 + gamma^2 alpha^2 - 2 alpha beta gamma - alpha^2 beta^2 gamma^2 [my identification]. The isolated '+ alpha beta gamma' looks like a stray or cancelled term. In words, he compares sin^2 a sin^2 b sin^2 c with the Gram determinant.
- He then writes the symmetric relation 1 - a^2 - b^2 - c^2 + 2abc = 0. With a, b, c cosines of three arcs, this holds exactly when the arcs satisfy x +/- y +/- z = 0 (mod 2 pi). It is Euler's symmetric, algebraic form of the cosine addition theorem; it is also the condition for a degenerate spherical triangle.
- The notes 'a = Secans, x = sin' suggest he is trying substitutions so that the same symmetric relation can be transferred to another function. Given the margin heading 'Die sqrt(1-x^4)', this points to the lemniscatic functions.

(2) MIDDLE: theta-level addition theorem for the lemniscatic functions. Context: the previous page has theta series and the integral dx/sqrt((1-xx)(1-mu mu xx)); the next page has a quintic transformation in P, Q, p, q.
- P, Q, p, q are Gauss's entire (theta-type) functions with sl phi = P(phi)/Q(phi) and cl phi = p(phi)/q(phi).
- The last line gives q(phi) = Q(90 deg - phi), where '90 deg' means the quarter period varpi/2. Correspondingly p(phi) = P(varpi/2 - phi), since cl phi = sl(varpi/2 - phi).
- He writes:
  q(A-B) Q(A+B) = QA QB qA qB - PA PB pA pB
  q(A-B) P(A+B) = PA qA QB pB + QA pA PB qB.
- Dividing the second by the first and then dividing through by QA qA QB qB gives sl(A+B) = (slA clB + clA slB)/(1 - slA slB clA clB). This is exactly Fagnano/Euler's lemniscatic addition theorem, so the pair of formulas is that theorem lifted to the numerator/denominator functions, with common factor q(A-B).

(3) VERTICAL MARGIN: values at a pole.
- Heading: 'Die sqrt(1-x^4)', followed by 'N. A 90 deg' and a word read as 'Aarau'.
- He writes s = infinity, i. Here s = sl and c = cl. From sl^2 + cl^2 + sl^2 cl^2 = 1, at a pole of sl one has cl = +/- i.
- He substitutes s' = infinity, c' = i into the addition formula: (s i + c inf)/(1 - s c i inf). Keeping the dominant terms gives c/(-s c i) = -1/(s i) = i/s.
- The analogous cl formula, (c c' - s s')/(1 + s c s' c'), gives -1/(c i) = i/c.
- This yields sl(phi + (1+i)varpi/2) = +/- i/sl(phi) and the companion relation for cl, i.e. the shift by the half-period at the pole. The written '-1/sc' and '-1/cc' are probably '-1/si' and '-1/ci'.
- An earlier attempt '(s inf + cc)/(1 - s inf cc)' appears to use a different assignment of the pole values.

'2-3+' at the foot is unrelated.
errors: The row 'alpha alpha beta beta + ... + alpha beta gamma - 2 alpha beta gamma - ...' contains a term +alpha beta gamma that does not belong to any natural product. It is apparently a stray or struck term; the correct difference (1-a^2)(1-b^2)(1-c^2) - Delta has only -2 alpha beta gamma.

The theta-level identities q(A-B)Q(A+B) = ... and q(A-B)P(A+B) = ... hold only with a normalization of P, Q, p, q, or else up to a constant factor. Setting B=0 requires Q(0) = 1 and q(0)·(...) consistency, i.e. q(0) = 1 in the chosen normalization. As written, no constant is shown, so the normalization is implicit. The ratio (the addition theorem for sl) is correct regardless.

Margin: the results '-1/sc' and '-1/cc' as transcribed do not follow from the substituted expression. The limit of (s i + c inf)/(1 - s c i inf) is -1/(s i) = i/s. Either the reading is wrong (likely '-1/si' and '-1/ci') or there is a slip.

results.what: (cos a - cos b cos c)^2 - sin^2 b sin^2 c = cos^2 a + cos^2 b + cos^2 c - 2 cos a cos b cos c - 1 (= -sin^2 b sin^2 c sin^2 A)
results.modern_name: Gram determinant / 'sine' of a spherical triangle (the quantity whose square root is the polar sine, Staudt's sine)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange (18th c.); von Staudt 1842 for the 'sine of the trihedral angle'

results.what: 1 - a^2 - b^2 - c^2 + 2abc = 0 as the symmetric algebraic form of the cosine addition theorem / degenerate triangle condition
results.modern_name: Euler's symmetric form of the addition theorem (algebraic relation among cos x, cos y, cos(x+y))

results.what: q(A-B)Q(A+B) = QA QB qA qB - PA PB pA pB and q(A-B)P(A+B) = PA qA QB pB + QA pA PB qB, with sl = P/Q, cl = p/q and q(phi) = Q(varpi/2 - phi)
results.modern_name: Addition formulas for theta functions (lemniscatic case), the theta-quotient lift of the lemniscatic addition theorem
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829, theta addition formulas); Gauss's lemniscatic P,Q functions are known from Werke III/X (c. 1798-1800)

results.what: At a pole of sl, cl = ±i; substituting into the addition theorem gives sl(phi + pole) = ± i/sl(phi)
results.modern_name: Half-period translation formula, analogue of sn(u+iK') = 1/(k sn u)
results.usually_credited_to: Abel/Jacobi (1827-29) in general; Gauss for the lemniscate (Werke III)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic theta-type functions P, Q, p, q and their addition and transformation formulas are documented in Werke III and X and discussed by Schlesinger. This page is scratch work in that known programme, alongside a routine spherical-trigonometry identity. Nothing on it goes beyond what is already attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: The top expansion equals alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2-2 alpha beta gamma-1 (should be 0).
The product sin^2a sin^2b sin^2c minus the Gram determinant equals the row on the page without the stray +alpha beta gamma (should be 0).
1-a^2-b^2-c^2+2abc=0 holds for a=cos x, b=cos y, c=cos(x+y) (should be 0).
The ratio of Gauss's two theta-level formulas is exactly the lemniscatic addition theorem sl(A+B)=(slA clB+clA slB)/(1-slA slB clA clB) (should be 0).
With cl = sqrt((1-sl^2)/(1+sl^2)) and sl -> infinity (cl -> ±i), the addition formula tends to ±i/s, i.e. sl(phi+pole) = ±i/sl(phi).

transcription_corrections: The row '[-1+-] alpha alpha beta beta + ...' is better read as a struck '1+' before alpha^2 beta^2 + beta^2 gamma^2 + alpha^2 gamma^2; the '+ alpha beta gamma' appears to be a stray or cancelled term.
'cc+c' is probably an aborted line (perhaps 'cos c^2 + ...'); its content is uncertain.
Margin: '-1/sc' and '-1/cc' are likely '-1/si' and '-1/ci' (equivalently i/s and i/c), as required by the limit of the preceding expression.
Margin: 'i' after 's = infinity' is the value cl = i at the pole of sl.
'90°' in 'q phi = Q(90° - phi)' denotes the lemniscatic quarter period varpi/2 (Gauss's habit of writing angle-like notation), not literally 90 degrees.
